glosses: to lie (to tell an intentional untruth)

A fretted stringed instrument, similar to the guitar, having a bowl-shaped body or soundbox; any of a wide variety of chordophones with a pear-shaped body and a neck whose upper surface is in the same plane as the soundboard, with strings along the neck and parallel to the soundboard.
To play on a lute, or as if on a lute.

examples.text: Knaves are men / That lute and flute fantastic tenderness.
in the air , her new voice luting soft

glosses: Thick sticky clay or cement used to close up a hole or gap, especially to make something air-tight.

examples.text: He employed a mixture of flour and white of egg spread upon a linen cloth to cement cracked glass vessels, and used other lutes for similar purposes.

glosses: A packing ring, as of rubber, for fruit jars, etc.
A straight-edged piece of wood for striking off superfluous clay from earth.
To fix or fasten something with lute.

examples.text: To protect everything till it dried, a man […] luted a big blue paper cap from a cracker, with meringue-cream, low down on Jevon's forehead.
